title: Equal pair response laws permit different site groups in three selected worm map models
abstract: We tested whether pair response laws identify shared release-site target groups in eight public worm brain maps. A fixed panel had 162 neurons. The model used unit target gains and equal, independent Bernoulli release at sites. A restricted exact search found four alternatives at four sources in maps 6, 7 and 8. Each alternative kept the source site count, source-to-target contact counts and all single-target and two-target response laws fixed for every release probability. It changed a three-target silence probability. At the assumed release probability 0.2, whole-source absolute probability gaps ranged from 0.000000935 to 0.04194. No member of this trade family was found in maps 1 through 5; this does not prove uniqueness. The result is an exact limit of inference under the model, not a measurement of release or neural coding. The alternatives do not preserve site size or geometry. Code, a proof, aggregate results, checks, a figure and pinned source retrieval steps support reproduction. External raw records and record-level alternatives remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Left: sources with an exact alternative in a restricted search. Right: different triple silence laws in a synthetic block with equal pair response laws. These are conditional model results.

citations.reason: Reuses the verified baseline-licensed 162-cell panel. Extends its release model to an inverse identifiability test. No code or site tables reused.
